name: example1
title: 1964: example 1, average of 100 logs
credit: First BASIC instruction manual, Dartmouth, May 1964, p. 21
program:
10 PRINT "AVERAGE OF 100 LOGS"
20 LET S = 0
30  FOR N = 1 to 100
40 LET S = S + FNL (N)
50 NEXT N
60 LET S = S/100
70 PRINT S
80 DEF FNL (Z) = LOG(Z)/LOG(10)
99 END

name: example2
title: 1964: example 2, quadratic equation
credit: First BASIC instruction manual, Dartmouth, May 1964, pp. 21-22
program:
5 PRINT "QUADRATIC EQUATION"
6 PRINT
10 READ A, B, C
20 LET D = B * B -4 * A * C
30 LET S = - B / (2 * A )
40 LET T = SQR(D) / (2 * A)
50 IF D = 0 THEN 100
60 IF D < 0 THEN 200
70 PRINT A, B, C, "TWO REAL ROOTS"
80 PRINT "ROOTS =" S + T, S - T
90 GOTO 300
100 PRINT A, B, C, "ONE ROOT"
110 PRINT "ROOT =" S
120 GOTO 300
200 PRINT A, B, C, "COMPLEX ROOTS"
210 PRINT "REAL PART=" S, "IMAGINARY PART=" T
300 PRINT
310 GOTO 10
400 DATA 1, -2, -3, 1, -4, 4, 1, 0, 2
999 END

name: example3
title: 1964: example 3, root of a function
credit: First BASIC instruction manual, Dartmouth, May 1964, p. 23
program:
10 PRINT "ROOT OF FUNCTION."
20 PRINT "FUNCTION IS - AT  0 AND + AT 1"
30 DEF FNF(Z) = Z↑5 +Z↑3 -1
40 LET X = 0
50 LET D = .5
60 LET Y = FNF(X)
70 IF Y = 0 THEN 200
80 IF Y > 0 THEN 150
90 LET X = X + D
100 GOTO 160
150 LET X = X - D
160 IF D <= .0001 THEN 200
170 LET D = D/2
180 GO TO 60
200 PRINT "ROOT =" X
999 END

name: primes
title: Primes
program:
10 REM Sieve of Eratosthenes: the primes below 100
20 N = 100
30 DIM C(N)
40 FOR I = 2 TO SQR(N)
50   IF C(I) = 1 THEN 90
60   FOR J = I * I TO N STEP I
70     C(J) = 1
80   NEXT J
90 NEXT I
100 K = 0
110 FOR I = 2 TO N
120   IF C(I) = 0 THEN PRINT I;: K = K + 1
130 NEXT I
140 PRINT
150 PRINT K; "PRIMES"
160 END

name: mandelbrot
title: Mandelbrot set
program:
10 REM The Mandelbrot set in ASCII
20 FOR Y = -12 TO 12
30   FOR X = -39 TO 39
40     C = X * .0458 - .5: D = Y * .08333
50     A = 0: B = 0
60     FOR I = 0 TO 15
70       T = A * A - B * B + C
80       B = 2 * A * B + D: A = T
90       IF A * A + B * B > 4 THEN 110
100     NEXT I
110     PRINT MID$(" .:-=+*#%@@@@@@@@", I + 1, 1);
120   NEXT X
130   PRINT
140 NEXT Y
150 END

name: guess
title: Guess the number
program:
10 REM Guess the number - an interactive game using RND and INPUT
20 N = INT(RND(1) * 100) + 1
30 PRINT "I AM THINKING OF A NUMBER BETWEEN 1 AND 100."
40 T = 0
50 INPUT "YOUR GUESS"; G
60 T = T + 1
70 IF G < N THEN PRINT "TOO LOW.": GOTO 50
80 IF G > N THEN PRINT "TOO HIGH.": GOTO 50
90 PRINT "YOU GOT IT IN"; T; "TRIES!"
100 END

name: lunar
title: Lunar Lander (game)
program:
10 PRINT TAB(33);"LUNAR"

120 L=0

140 A=120:V=1:M=33000:N=16500:G=1E-03:Z=1.8

160 IF M-N<1E-03 THEN 240
170 IF T<1E-03 THEN 150
180 S=T: IF M>=N+S*K THEN 200
190 S=(M-N)/K

210 IF V<=0 THEN 230
220 IF J<0 THEN 370
230 GOSUB 330: GOTO 160
240 PRINT "FUEL OUT AT";L;"SECONDS":S=(-V+SQR(V*V+2*A*G))/G

name: diamond

program:

8 FOR L=1 TO Q
10 X=1:Y=R:Z=2
20 FOR N=X TO Y STEP Z

28 FOR M=1 TO Q
29 C=1
30 FOR A=1 TO N

83 IF X<>1 THEN 95
85 X=R-2:Y=1:Z=-2
90 GOTO 20
95 NEXT L
99 END

name: classic/tpk

program:
10 REM THE TPK ALGORITHM OF KNUTH AND TRABB PARDO, IN 1964 BASIC
20 REM SOURCE: D. E. KNUTH AND L. TRABB PARDO, THE EARLY DEVELOPMENT
30 REM OF PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES, STAN-CS-76-562 (1976), P. 3, WHERE
40 REM IT IS GIVEN IN ALGOL 60. THEY DO NOT WRITE IT IN BASIC.
50 REM READ ELEVEN NUMBERS, THEN FOR EACH IN REVERSE ORDER PRINT
60 REM I AND F(A(I)), OR TOO LARGE IF F(A(I)) > 400.
70 REM INPUT: THEIR EXAMPLE, A(0) TO A(10) = 1 1.5 2 2.25 2.5 2.75
80 REM 3 3.25 3.5 4.5 5.5, IN THE DATA AT LINE 300.
90 REM CHANGES FROM THE ALGOL, AND WHY (MAY 1964 MANUAL PAGES):
100 REM - READ AND DATA FOR READ(A[I]): THERE IS NO OTHER INPUT (P. 14)
110 REM - T*T*T FOR T TO THE 3RD: A POWER TAKES THE ABSOLUTE VALUE
120 REM   OF ITS BASE, SO X*X*X IS THE RULE FOR A CUBE (P. 5)
130 REM - IF ... THEN A LINE NUMBER AND GO TO FOR IF-THEN-ELSE (P. 11)
140 REM - DIM A(10) FOR REAL ARRAY A[0:10]
150 REM - THE FUNCTION IS FNF, ITS ARGUMENT T (P. 13)
200 DIM A(10)
210 DEF FNF(T) = SQR(ABS(T)) + 5*T*T*T
220 FOR I = 0 TO 10
230 READ A(I)
240 NEXT I
250 FOR I = 10 TO 0 STEP -1
260 LET Y = FNF(A(I))
270 IF Y > 400 THEN 295
280 PRINT I, Y
290 GO TO 299
295 PRINT I, "TOO LARGE"
299 NEXT I

999 END

name: games/word
title: Word
program:
2 PRINT TAB(33);"WORD"
3 PRINT TAB(15);"CREATIVE COMPUTING  MORRISTOWN, NEW JERSEY"
4 PRINT: PRINT: PRINT
5 DIM S(7),A(7),L(7),D(7),P(7)
10 PRINT "I AM THINKING OF A WORD -- YOU GUESS IT.  I WILL GIVE YOU"
15 PRINT "CLUES TO HELP YOU GET IT.  GOOD LUCK!!": PRINT: PRINT
20 REM
30 PRINT: PRINT: PRINT "YOU ARE STARTING A NEW GAME..."
35 RESTORE
40 READ N
50 C=INT(RND(1)*N+1)
60 FOR I=1 TO C
70 READ S$
80 NEXT I
90 G=0
95 S(0)=LEN(S$)
100 FOR I=1 TO LEN(S$): S(I)=ASC(MID$(S$,I,1)): NEXT I
110 FOR I=1 TO 5
120 A(I)=45
130 NEXT I
140 FOR J=1 TO 5
144 P(J)=0
146 NEXT J
150 PRINT "GUESS A FIVE LETTER WORD";
160 INPUT L$
170 G=G+1
172 IF S$=L$ THEN 500
173 FOR I=1 TO 7: P(I)=0: NEXT I
175 L(0)=LEN(L$)
180 FOR I=1 TO LEN(L$): L(I)=ASC(MID$(L$,I,1)): NEXT I
190 IF L(1)=63 THEN 300
200 IF L(0)<>5 THEN 400
205 M=0: Q=1
210 FOR I=1 TO 5
220 FOR J=1 TO 5
230 IF S(I)<>L(J) THEN 260
231 P(Q)=L(J)
232 Q=Q+1
233 IF I<>J THEN 250
240 A(J)=L(J)
250 M=M+1
260 NEXT J
265 NEXT I
270 A(0)=5
272 P(0)=M
275 A$="": FOR I=1 TO A(0): A$=A$+CHR$(A(I)): NEXT I
277 P$="": FOR I=1 TO P(0): P$=P$+CHR$(P(I)): NEXT I
280 PRINT "THERE WERE";M;"MATCHES AND THE COMMON LETTERS WERE...";P$
285 PRINT "FROM THE EXACT LETTER MATCHES, YOU KNOW................";A$
286 IF A$=S$ THEN 500
287 IF M>1 THEN 289
288 PRINT: PRINT "IF YOU GIVE UP, TYPE '?' FOR YOUR NEXT GUESS."
289 PRINT
290 GOTO 150
300 S$="": FOR I=1 TO 7: S$=S$+CHR$(S(I)): NEXT I
310 PRINT "THE SECRET WORD IS ";S$: PRINT
320 GOTO 30
400 PRINT "YOU MUST GUESS A 5 LETTER WORD.  START AGAIN."
410 PRINT: G=G-1: GOTO 150
500 PRINT "YOU HAVE GUESSED THE WORD.  IT TOOK";G;"GUESSES!": PRINT
510 INPUT "WANT TO PLAY AGAIN";Q$
520 IF Q$="YES" THEN 30
530 DATA 12,"DINKY","SMOKE","WATER","GRASS","TRAIN","MIGHT","FIRST"
540 DATA "CANDY","CHAMP","WOULD","CLUMP","DOPEY"
999 END
